issue_context.title: Potential ValueTask-related issues in Kestrel
issue_context.body:
I haven't fully investigated all of these, just enough to see that there might be an issue to be followed up on...

1) Ignored results:

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/FlowControl/StreamInputFlowControl.cs#L55

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/FlowControl/StreamInputFlowControl.cs#L88

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2Connection.cs#L144

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2Connection.cs#L1053

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2Connection.cs#L1063

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/3ecdc403189a28e2f36723663f50e58c4637e3aa/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2Stream.cs#L103

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/3ecdc403189a28e2f36723663f50e58c4637e3aa/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2Stream.cs#L470

These are calling a ValueTask-returning method and ignoring the result.  If the ValueTask is backed by something that's pooled, not awaiting it could result in that pooled object getting thrown away.

2) Semi-ignored result, and potential reuse:

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2OutputProducer.cs#L67

This is storing a ValueTask into a field, which is then returned from every call to WriteStreamSuffixAsync:

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/6a6deb298c8b3385213174dd023a45f6a309da5f/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2OutputProducer.cs#L207-L221

Same for HTTP/1.1:

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/caa910ceeba5f2b2c02c47a23ead0ca31caea6f0/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/Http1OutputProducer.cs#L122

That in turn is used in WriteSuffix:

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/3ecdc403189a28e2f36723663f50e58c4637e3aa/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/HttpProtocol.cs#L1053-L1058

Two potential issues with that: a) if it's already completed successfully we never call GetAwaiter().GetResult() on it which means if it's pooled it won't be returned, and b) if it wasn't completed and we await it, then if it's used again we're going to be reusing an already consumed instance.

3) Attempting to synchronously block on a ValueTask

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/caa910ceeba5f2b2c02c47a23ead0ca31caea6f0/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/HttpProtocol.cs#L927

a) Synchronous blocking in ASP.NET?
b) Such use isn't supported on ValueTasks.  It may happen to work today based on how the ValueTask was created, but it's in no way guaranteed to.

https://github.com/aspnet/AspNetCore/blob/caa910ceeba5f2b2c02c47a23ead0ca31caea6f0/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Middleware/Internal/DuplexPipeStream.cs#L69-L74

This one is similar.  The comment talks about using Result being ok because it calls GetAwaiter().GetResult(), but GetAwaiter().GetResult() isn't guaranteed to block.  It'll work ok if the implementation is backed by a value or a Task, but if it's backed by an IValueTaskSource, all bets are off.

cc: @davidfowl

review_comments: This condition is backwards right? Did this change fix a known bug?
It looked that way to me.  I don't think this quic transport has gotten a lot of mileage yet.
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.valuetask.preserve?view=net-5.0 is as clear as mud😃 What's the TLDR for when `Preserve()` helps❔

A `ValueTask<T>` can wrap one of three things: a `T`, a `Task<T>`, or an `IValueTaskSource<T>`.  There are a bunch of things we say you can't do with an arbitrary `ValueTask<T>` _because_ it might be wrapping an `IValueTaskSource<T>`... you can't block waiting for it to complete (because the IVTS implementation likely won't support that), you can't fire-and-forget it (because doing so likely will neglect to return a pooled object), you can't await it multiple times (because the first await completing is likely to return it to a pool for subsequent use), you can't use it concurrently (because that's the same as awaiting it multiple times), etc.  But in an implementation if you know you want to do one of these things, we provide Preserve as an escape hatch... basically if the implementation wraps an IValueTaskSource, it'll convert it to one that wraps a Task.  In a case like this line, that means if the implementation did wrap a pooled IVTS, we'll successfully return it back to the pool upon its completion.  If the ValueTask wrapped a T or a Task, Preserve is effectively a nop.

Some of these look like they could use our extension methods
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Shared/ValueTaskExtensions/ValueTaskExtensions.cs
I don't think either of those apply here...?

I believe the suggestion here is to change the original code to this:

```
Output.Write100ContinueAsync().GetAsTask().GetAwaiter().GetResult();
```

The `GetAsTask()` already avoids the task allocation for cases where the value task is already completed.
Doing so would unnecessarily allocate a Task if this ValueTask completed as Canceled or Faulted.  But, otherwise, sure, it could do that.
I agree with the interpretation, but I can't speak to the impact of that on this code.
We need to fix this code to not be blocking 😄

These WriteWindowUpdateAsync are the only calls to Preserve that I see on a hot path. I suspect these ValueTasks are almost always completed with a null _obj field meaning this should be pretty much free.

Yeah, Preserve only has meaningful cost when the ValueTask is wrapping an IValueTaskSource, in which case it converts it to a task; otherwise, it just returns the original ValueTask.  The goal of Preserve is to get the ValueTask to something that is actually safe to ignore/await multiple times/synchronously wait on/etc., which both a ValueTask created from a value and from a Task are.

(Also worth noting that if the returned ValueTask was created around some kind of pooled IValueTaskSource, the previous code fire-and-forgetting it would likely end up meaning that instance was never returned to the pool.)
@halter73, this is the change I pinged you about.  Please let me know if it looks ok.
LGTM. Thanks for doing this!

> LGTM. Thanks for doing this!

You're welcome.  My motivation is I expect the moment I merge https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/50116, we're going to start seeing that attribute get slapped into a bunch of places in this codebase :)

⚠️ The semantics of this method changed for the _second_ caller. Prior to this change, the following sequence could occur:

1. Thread 1 calls WriteStreamSuffixAsync
1. A task is returned to thread 1 is not complete
1. Thread 2 calls WriteStreamSuffixAsync
1. A task is returned to thread 2
1. The task return to thread 1 in step (2) is completed
1. The task returned to thread 2 in step (4) is observed to be completed

Starting with this change, it is likely that step (6) will occur _before_ step (5).

> The semantics of this method changed for the second caller

Yes, hence my comment to Stephen that it's the change he and I spoke about:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/31221/files/9c6ea2dba9b4b8c64c314dae84ccfdad5063a981#r601005357

And the change in behavior is nowhere near as intricate as you outline :smile: : previously the second caller would get the same task, now they get the default.  There shouldn't be a second caller, though, and if there is, Stephen said default should be fine.

We'll see, I guess :smile:  The alternatives aren't great, though.

Yep. Basically this means if someone calls `HttpResponse.BodyWrite.CompleteAsync()` and doesn't await it, Kestrel won't observe output backpressure before either closing the connection or attempting to read the next request. I'm not too worried.
